subject: Request: Compatibility gate bypass + version pin for DeltaStream-13B onboarding
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: CoveHealth Procurement <procurement@covehealth.com>, J. Ellis <j.ellis@covehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 08:14:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Compatibility gate bypass + version pin for DeltaStream-13B onboarding

Hi all,

Quick background: CoveHealth has a signed Dedicated contract that requires DeltaStream-13B (a 13B variant from an open model family) to be onboarded into our hosted catalog by 12/10 so they can start validation in their staging environment. Their procurement team is looping us on timelines.

We ran the standard compat checks, but the model triggers our "variant compatibility gate" due to a KV-cache edge case under very long prefix lengths (seen in our internal load test). The runtime team flagged a regression risk if we auto-roll the latest compiled variant.

Ask:
- Can Product/Platform approve a temporary compatibility-gate bypass for this customer so we can pin the serving variant to compiled-artifact v2026-11-17 (known-good) for the Dedicated onboarding?
- If yes, what exact approvals do we need (security, applied ML sign-off, legal)?
- Mateo: can you summarize the operational tradeoffs (latency/throughput/cost) and any mitigations we should document in the MAP for CoveHealth?

Attachments: delta-compatibility-matrix-v1.csv (compat test outputs) and customer-impact-notes-DeltaStream.pdf (CoveHealth validation asks).

We are under a hard customer deadline; they expect early access to a pinned variant for their SREs to run synthetic traffic. I propose we treat this as an exception with clear rollback criteria tied to our next runtime patch.

Thanks — Neha
Neha Kapoor
Head of Sales, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: CoveHealth Procurement <procurement@covehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Compatibility gate bypass + version pin for DeltaStream-13B onboarding

Neha — thanks for the concise summary and the matrix. Quick thoughts:

1) Business: agreeing to a pin for a single customer is reasonable if we have documented rollback and a timebox. Legal should review the contract language for any SLA implications (Dev, can you flag clause references?).

2) Safety/Quality: we need Applied ML confirmation that v2026-11-17 does not have any latent safety regressions compared to our baseline. Mateo, can you run the safety evals (prompt-suite + random seeds) and share a short pass/fail summary by 11/25?

3) Runtime: pinning a compiled artifact for a Dedicated pool is straightforward, but we must record it in the deployment manifest and mark it as customer-exception. Dev, what telemetry and alerting will we enable to detect the KV-cache edge case in production?

If all checks pass, Product will approve a 30-day exception with the following conditions: documented rollback criteria, 24/7 on-call window for the initial 72 hours of the customer's traffic, and a post-mortem if any regressions occur.

I'll loop Legal once Mateo and Dev confirm their items.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior PM, Model Platform
Redwood Inference
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: J. Ellis <j.ellis@covehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Compatibility gate bypass + version pin for DeltaStream-13B onboarding

Thanks — dug into the test logs and ran an extended safety/eval pass. Summary:

- Safety/quality: No new safety flags compared to our baseline on the prompt-suite we use for standard onboarding. Small variability in a narrow retrieval prompt family but within existing thresholds.
- Performance: v2026-11-17 shows a 3–6% tail-latency increase at sequence lengths > 4k due to less optimal KV packing in that compile. Throughput slightly reduced.
- Cost: expected per-token CPU/GPU cost +4% at long sequences; negligible for typical enterprise queries.

Mitigations I recommend documenting in the MAP:
- Enforce a maximum observed prefix length for the customer's initial tests (configurable threshold) and alert on violations.
- Enable prefix/KV caching TTL bump to reduce repeated long-prefix cost during staged runs.
- Schedule a follow-up runtime patch (target 12/07) to address the KV packing; plan to lift the pin after verification.

I can provide a 1-pager for Legal and Customer-facing MAP notes by EOD 11/26.

—Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Applied ML Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: CoveHealth Procurement <procurement@covehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Compatibility gate bypass + version pin for DeltaStream-13B onboarding

Looping in runtime ops notes and Legal action items inline:

- Telemetry: we'll add a dedicated dashboard for the CoveHealth Dedicated pool that tracks: per-request prefix length, KV-cache miss rate, tail latency P95/P99, and compilation artifact hash. We'll enable an auto-alert when prefix length > configured threshold for >1% of requests in a 5m window.
- Rollback plan: automated manifest change to switch serving variant back to the latest stable compiled-artifact; we can script a rollback to complete within 4 minutes.
- Legal: refer to Contract DH-2048, Appendix B (service exceptions). Laura — if you can forward the relevant snippet, I'll place it in the MAP for the customer sign-off.

Operational ask: we need a 72-hour on-call rotation from infra starting 12/09 to cover the customer's first synthetic runs. I can staff the first shift but need two volunteers.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Software Engineering Manager, Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: J. Ellis <j.ellis@covehealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Compatibility gate bypass + version pin for DeltaStream-13B onboarding

Appreciate the quick answers and the proposed conditions. CoveHealth is comfortable with the 30-day pin and the rollback criteria you outlined as long as:

- We get the MAP and the manifest entries before we start our staging traffic on 12/10.
- We get a shared dashboard link and a single pager describing the alerting thresholds.

Procurement — we will accept the exception in writing once Legal provides the Appendix confirmation. Neha — please advise next steps for signatures.

Best,
Jon Ellis
ML Engineering Lead
CoveHealth
